result: At the pinned rust-sdk commit, TaskServer::call_tool reads RequestContext::client_capabilities() for each call. The same test file contains a tasks-capable client case that receives CreateTaskResult, a plain-client case that receives the synchronous sum result instead, and a dispatch guard that rejects an attempted task result to a non-declaring client with MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY. This is concrete source-level and end-to-end test evidence that declared client capability changes materially gate server behavior and that dispatch independently enforces the negative path.
scope_guard: The inspected tests use separate server instances for the positive and negative client cases. They do not directly exercise two differently-capable clients or capability changes against one long-lived server instance, so stale cross-request capability reuse is not ruled out by this slice. No claim is made about ChatGPT or scheduled-Chat advertised capabilities, deployed transport persistence, process-loss durability, external storage, quota-zero deployment, or end-to-end richer-mode parity.
remaining_unresolved_child: Find or construct exact public-source evidence that alternates capability declarations across requests or clients on one long-lived server/session boundary, proving request-scoped capability state is not stale or reused across requests.
continuation: Next invocation: preserve CLEAN bootstrap and pinned rust-sdk commit 4a738b9dd99eaca418b614afa433a0cbdaf8d056. Inspect exactly one focused service/transport test or implementation path that demonstrates how peer/client capabilities are bound to RequestContext across multiple requests on a long-lived service, preferring an existing test over broad discovery. Record exact path/blob evidence and leave product/deployment/quota/end-to-end parity unresolved unless directly proven.
